comments.body: I wonder why Claude can't do this in unity with mcp. Looks like threejs works better as unity mcp. It's crazy

replies.author: guanzo91
replies.body: Yeah i dont get it. At the end of the day, it's just code. It should be portable to any other game engine. Especially with LLM assistance.

replies.author: NoBackupDev
replies.body: I think LLMs just dont have a good understanding of Unity and Unreal. I've ported my own games from threejs and UE to Godot, and the code migration is mostly one shot. The visuals take much more time to set up.

replies.author: soldture
replies.body: Because Unity handles a significant part of its development through a UI rather than just through code like Three.js, Godot is as far as I know better handled by LLMs than Unity

comments.author: CashFirm573
comments.body: I love this, been watching ya progression, if there one thing I'd recommend, dude switch to rust/bevy and it will blow away three.js, cause three.js has a ceiling and you're going to hit it and have major performance issues and also you can get way better visuals with bevy.

replies.author: Efficient_Ad8214
replies.body: Worth checking! Thanks for the feedback

replies.author: CashFirm573
replies.body: From the testing I've done it does decent at simple projects but issue is how it's rendered, there are 2 options really and those aren't what I would call high-end for 3d project, if it was 2D or low poly sure, be fine but soon as you try to push the limits into say AAA unreal engine style the performance bottoms out and it starts to crack, and it also can't do visual quality it just can't three.js is cool for tech demos that's about it, I would never use it in a real project outside of web development, AI can do amazing job of getting rather high but it's still going to hit a wall.
